---
title: Add the player
description: Play private and public videos in your pages with the clipmux-player element, which renews tokens while it plays.
---

`<clipmux-player>` is a web component from `@clipmux/player`: Video.js 10's
skin around hls.js. It plays a video by its playback ID, shows the poster,
subtitles and chapters, and asks your backend for a new token whenever the
old one runs out, without losing the viewer's place. It works in plain HTML
and in any framework.

## Before you start

- A video with a playback ID, `pid_…`, from your `asset` callback or
  `GET /v1/assets/{id}`.
- For a private video, a route on your backend that decides who may watch.
  The [quickstart](/docs/build/quickstart)'s `clipmuxHandler` gives you one
  at `/api/clipmux/playback`.
- The package:

<Tabs items={['npm', 'pnpm']}>
<Tab value="npm">

```bash
npm i @clipmux/player
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="pnpm">

```bash
pnpm add @clipmux/player
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Play with a session URL [#play-with-a-session-url]

The shortest way is `session-url`. The page needs only the playback ID:

```html
<script type="module">
  import '@clipmux/player/element'
</script>
<clipmux-player playback-id="pid_…" session-url="/api/clipmux/playback"></clipmux-player>
```

The element POSTs `{"playback_id": "pid_…", "native": false}` to that URL.
Your backend checks the viewer, from its own session, and answers with a
playback session:

```json
{
  "playback_id": "pid_…",
  "base_url": "https://media.example.com",
  "token": "eyJ…",
  "expires_at": "2026-11-18T10:15:00.000Z",
  "poster_url": "https://media.example.com/v/eyJ…/pid_…/poster.jpg",
  "title": "Lesson 42",
  "duration_seconds": 612.4,
  "tracks": [{ "id": "trk_…", "kind": "chapters", "source": "generated", "status": "ready" }]
}
```

The `/playback` route of `clipmuxHandler` answers exactly this, from your
`playback` callback. It includes `tracks`, `title` and `duration_seconds`
only when the callback returns the video as well, `{ viewerId, asset }`;
with only the playback ID, the session has no tracks, so the player finds
no chapters. To build it yourself in Node, return
`clipmux.playback.session(asset, { viewerId, native })`. The player:

- plays from `base_url` with `token`;
- shows `poster_url`, unless you set `poster`;
- marks the chapters of the first ready chapters track, unless you set
  `chapters-track`;
- POSTs to the same URL again whenever the token expires.

A `401` or `403` from your route fires `clipmux-denied` and stops playback.
Any other failure fires `clipmux-error` with its `status`. The answer in use
is on `player.session`.

## Play with getToken

If your page already knows the media origin, or you have your own token
route, set `getToken` instead. The element calls it for the first token and
for every renewal:

```ts
import '@clipmux/player/element'

const player = document.querySelector('clipmux-player')!
player.getToken = async ({ playbackId, native }) => {
  const res = await fetch(`/api/playback-token?playback_id=${playbackId}&native=${native}`)
  return res.ok ? res.text() : null // null denies
}
```

```html
<clipmux-player base-url="https://media.example.com" playback-id="pid_…"></clipmux-player>
```

Return the token as a string, or `null` to refuse; `null` fires
`clipmux-denied`. Your route signs the token after its own access check; see
[Sign playback tokens](/docs/build/play/sign-tokens). If you set
`getToken` as well as `session-url`, `getToken` is used for renewals.

A public playback ID needs no token: set `base-url` and `playback-id` and
leave `getToken` unset. See [Public videos](/docs/build/play/public-videos).

## How renewal works

The token rides in the URL path. When it expires, delivery answers `401
token_expired`. The player asks for a new token once, puts it into that
request and every later one, and retries, so the viewer sees nothing.

Where the browser plays HLS itself, with no Media Source (iOS before 17.1,
AirPlay), the player can't swap the token mid-video. The element tells your
backend: `native: true` in the session request, or in `getToken`'s
argument. Pass it through when you sign, and the token is signed to outlive
the session. If you drop it, Safari before 17.1 stops when the first token
expires. iOS 17.1 and later play through hls.js and renew like any other
browser.

## Attributes and properties

<TypeTable
  type={{
    'playback-id': { type: 'string', description: 'The playback ID to play, pid_….' },
    'session-url': { type: 'string', description: 'Your backend route that answers with a playback session. With it, base-url is not needed.' },
    'base-url': { type: 'string', description: 'The media origin, for example https://media.example.com. Needed without session-url.' },
    poster: { type: 'string', description: 'A poster image URL. Overrides the session\'s poster_url.' },
    'chapters-track': { type: 'string', description: 'The ID of a ready chapters track, trk_…, to mark on the time slider.' },
    autoplay: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Passed to the media element.' },
    muted: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Passed to the media element.' },
  }}
/>

Properties, set from script:

<TypeTable
  type={{
    getToken: { type: '({ playbackId, native }) => Promise<string | null>', description: 'Called for the first token and every renewal. null refuses.' },
    token: { type: 'string', description: 'A token to start with. Without getToken it can\'t be renewed.' },
    hls: { type: 'Record<string, unknown>', description: 'Extra hls.js options. Set it before the first load.' },
    session: { type: 'PlaybackSession | null', description: 'Read only. The session-url answer in use.' },
    chapters: { type: 'PlayerChapter[]', description: 'Read only. The chapters, in seconds, once clipmux-chapters has fired.' },
    media: { type: 'HTMLVideoElement | null', description: 'Read only. The inner <hlsjs-video> element.' },
  }}
/>

Set `getToken` rather than `token` when you can, so the first token can be
a native one when the browser needs it.

`player.media` is the `<hlsjs-video>` element. Read `currentTime`,
`paused`, `ended`, `duration` and `readyState` from it, and listen for its
media events (`timeupdate`, `ended` and so on), to resume where a viewer
left off or to report progress.

## Events [#events]

They bubble, and they are typed on `HTMLElementEventMap`, so
`player.addEventListener('clipmux-chapters', (e) => e.detail.chapters)`
needs no cast.

| Event | `detail` | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `clipmux-token` | `{ token }` | A new token is in use. |
| `clipmux-denied` | `{}` | Your backend said no (`null` from `getToken`, or `401` or `403` from `session-url`), or delivery answered `403`. Playback stops. |
| `clipmux-error` | `{ status, track? }` | Something failed. `status` is the HTTP status, or `0` for a network or media error. `track` is set when a track's file failed to load. |
| `clipmux-chapters` | `{ chapters }` | The chapters track loaded. Times are in seconds. |

`clipmux-denied` means the viewer may not watch: show your own sign-in or
enrol state, not an error. A `clipmux-error` with `status: 404` means the
playback ID was revoked or never existed, so show that the video was
removed.

## React and Next.js [#react-and-nextjs]

The element needs the DOM and Media Source, so a server render must not load
it. Import it in an effect, and import the JSX types once:

```tsx title="app/lessons/[id]/player.tsx"
'use client'
import type { ClipMuxPlayerElement } from '@clipmux/player/element' // types only
import type {} from '@clipmux/player/react' // JSX types only, no React dependency
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react'

export function Player({ playbackId }: { playbackId: string }) {
  const player = useRef<ClipMuxPlayerElement>(null)
  useEffect(() => {
    import('@clipmux/player/element')
    const el = player.current
    const onDenied = () => location.assign('/enrol')
    el?.addEventListener('clipmux-denied', onDenied)
    return () => el?.removeEventListener('clipmux-denied', onDenied)
  }, [])
  return <clipmux-player ref={player} playback-id={playbackId} session-url="/api/clipmux/playback" />
}
```

`@clipmux/player/react` types the attributes, the `token`, `getToken` and
`hls` properties and the `onclipmux-*` handlers, for React 18 and 19. The
listener goes on a ref because React 19 attaches an `onclipmux-denied` prop
only to an element it creates in the browser, not to one it hydrates from
server-rendered HTML, which is what a Next.js page's first load does (React
18 never attaches them).
[`examples/nextjs-lms`](https://github.com/visheshgubrani/clipmux/blob/main/examples/nextjs-lms/app/lessons/%5Bid%5D/lesson-video.tsx)
does the same for both elements. In Next.js, `router.refresh()` from a `clipmux-denied` handler re-renders the
page's locked state.

To set `getToken` from React, wait until the element is defined, then set it
on a ref:

```tsx title="player.tsx"
'use client'
import type {} from '@clipmux/player/react'
import type { ClipMuxPlayerElement } from '@clipmux/player/element'
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'

export function Player({ baseUrl, playbackId }: { baseUrl: string; playbackId: string }) {
  const ref = useRef<ClipMuxPlayerElement>(null)
  const [defined, setDefined] = useState(false)
  useEffect(() => {
    import('@clipmux/player/element').then(() => setDefined(true))
  }, [])
  useEffect(() => {
    const el = ref.current
    if (!defined || !el) return
    el.getToken = async ({ native }) => {
      const res = await fetch(`/api/playback-token?playback_id=${playbackId}&native=${native}`)
      return res.ok ? res.text() : null
    }
  }, [defined, playbackId])
  return <clipmux-player ref={ref} base-url={baseUrl} playback-id={playbackId} />
}
```

Video.js 10.2's own declaration files don't all type-check, so keep
`"skipLibCheck": true` in `tsconfig.json`. Most templates have it already.

## Subtitles and chapters [#subtitles-and-chapters]

Subtitles need no attribute. A ready subtitles track is listed in the HLS
master playlist, so it appears in the player's captions menu, and its files
load with the same token as the video.

Chapters are never in the master playlist. With `session-url`, the player
marks the first ready chapters track by itself. Otherwise, name the track:

```html
<clipmux-player base-url="https://media.example.com" playback-id="pid_…" chapters-track="trk_…"></clipmux-player>
```

The player fetches the track's WebVTT with the playback token and divides
the seek bar into chapter segments. Hover or scrub to see the title and
timestamp. When the track loads, the player fires `clipmux-chapters` and
fills `player.chapters`. Times there are in seconds; the API's `chapters` on a
track are in milliseconds. See
[Subtitles and transcripts](/docs/build/captions/subtitles) and
[Chapters](/docs/build/captions/chapters).

## Theming

Set `--media-accent-color` on the player or an ancestor to colour the
controls:

```css
clipmux-player {
  --media-accent-color: #e11d48;
}
```

The player is 16:9 and fills its container's width.

## Content-Security-Policy [#content-security-policy]

A page with the player must allow, besides its own origin:

| Directive | Sources | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `connect-src` | the media origin | playlists, segments, keys and subtitles |
| `media-src` | `blob:` and the media origin | Media Source playback, and native HLS |
| `img-src` | the media origin | the poster |
| `style-src` | `'unsafe-inline'` | Video.js injects its skin's styles |

`npx @clipmux/node doctor` prints the exact origins. hls.js runs on the main
thread, so no `worker-src` is needed.

## Check it works

Open the page with the player and watch the browser's network panel:

- `master.m3u8`, then playlists, `key/…` and `.m4s` segments answer `200`.
  The video plays.
- Your session route answers `403`, and `clipmux-denied` fires: your
  `playback` callback returned `null`.
- Delivery answers `403 denied`: the token was signed with the wrong key or
  for another playback ID. Run `npx @clipmux/node doctor`.
- Requests are blocked in the console with a CSP message: add the origins
  above.
